title: French students protest learning conditions and teacher shortages in Saint-Denis
seoTitle: Saint-Denis student protest for school conditions

tea.why: Students are protesting over poor learning conditions, teacher shortages, classroom overcrowding, and dilapidated facilities.
tea.want: They demand more staff, replacement of absent teachers, better infrastructure, smaller classes, and Parcoursup system overhauls.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Activist Greta Thunberg joined students outside Lycee Paul Eluard in Saint-Denis amid ongoing nationwide school protests.

summary: French high school students have organized a nationwide movement spanning several weeks to protest against poor learning conditions, teacher shortages, dilapidated school infrastructure, and classroom overcrowding. The movement began at Lycée Saint-Exupéry before spreading to hundreds of schools across France, including high schools in Saint-Denis where students blockaded entrances, sat down on pavements, and held demonstrations. The protesters demand the replacement of absent teachers, improved heating, smaller class sizes, and an overhaul of the online college application system. Education Minister Edouard Geffray stated that roughly 200 schools were closed during the recent mobilization days. The demonstrations have faced a heavy police response involving tear gas and charges, prompting intense debate over the methods used by law enforcement, while the government has promised to address the students' concerns.
demands: Overhaul of the Parcoursup college application system
response: Education Minister Edouard Geffray stated around 200 schools were closed due to safety precautions along march routes. The government suspended stun grenade use after injuries. Authorities deployed riot police who used tear gas and charges, leading to thousands of arrests and hundreds of injuries.

arrests.text: nearly 7,000 people have been taken into custody

updates.text: Students and professors gathered outside Lycée Saint-Exupéry to demand increased staffing.
A 15-year-old lost a hand to a stun grenade, and other teenagers suffered facial injuries during police interventions.
Students at Lycée Suger in Saint-Denis sat down at closed school gates behind teacher banners.
Greta Thunberg joined a demonstration outside Lycee Paul Eluard in Saint-Denis supporting the student movement.

sources.title: Greta Thunberg joins French teens on new day of school protests
